row.scenario: slice-2 query fixture: CJK queries of 1, 2 and 3+ characters against 用户喜欢简洁的回答
row.required_outcome: One- and two-character queries go through the bounded scoped substring pass and find the note (partial reported when the scan cap is hit; not on a corpus this small); three-or-more-character queries reach the trigram table, in Devanagari too; an alias hit is reported as `alias`; complete Chinese retrieval is never claimed from unicode61 alone. Supports matrix row 12.

design: §5 step 4 (03 rev 7.8, 09 §6.5): a term of three or more characters carrying a character of a script unicode61 cannot split into words (CJK among them, and Devanagari, whose words it breaks at every vowel sign) is matched exactly on the unicode61 table and as a substring on the trigram tables, which hold titles, aliases and tags and the body of every chunk carrying such a character — a mixed Latin and Chinese chunk included; one- and two-character queries use a bounded scoped substring pass; return `partial: true` when a scan cap is hit
notes_for_implementer: Four notes: the target (body 用户喜欢简洁的回答, alias 简洁), a CJK decoy about apples, an English decoy, and a Latin note with a Chinese phrase in its body (note 004, added by LQ17). Lengths are in characters, not bytes: 答 is one character and three UTF-8 bytes, so a byte-counting router would send it to the trigram table and a 2-character query to `unicode61`, where it matches nothing — the lengths here catch that. The design gives the substring pass no MatchReason, so steps 1–3 check the id and `partial: false` only; step 4's alias hit is `alias`; steps 5 and 6 (3+ characters inside the body's one CJK run) include `trigram` wherever the term stands in the run — `用户喜欢` begins it and `简洁的回答` ends it, and a CJK term is never a prefix query (09 §6.5.2) — and step 7 is the exact title. Step 13 searches `说明写成` inside note 004's `发布说明写成要点`: a chunk that carries an unsegmented character keeps its body in the trigram table even when most of it is Latin. Step 14 searches `दोस्त` (friend) in note 005's `दोस्तों` (friends'), added by LQ17's repair round 1: unicode61 breaks a Devanagari word at every vowel sign, so the script counts as unsegmented (09 §6.5.1) and its body is in the trigram table; the virama inside `दोस्त` is no letter, so the query is a literal and the stem is found inside the inflected form as `phrase`. Step 8 is the full-width punctuation and NFKC case: ｑｕｉｃｋ must normalize to `quick` and find the English decoy. Step 9 mixes scripts in one query and returns both matching notes by the union rule.
